utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will wait -- before the witness, are there any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Will there be any preliminaries or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then, please, the witness waits outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Never miss a thing. It's Monday morning. Yes, Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. The case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Oric, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, counsel for the Prosecution, and also good morning to the Defence. I am here together with co-counsel, Miss Patricia Sellers and our case manager, Mrs. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I thank you, and good morning to you and to your team. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I am Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones, I appear as Defence counsel for Mr. Naser Oric. With us here we have our legal assistant, Adisa Mehic, and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts. Good morning to my colleagues of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We end up with new developments last week with a view to the time needed for the witness Bogilovic and that is why we decided and planned to reschedule the coming witness, Brkic, for a later moment in time and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Coming witness -- one moment. I'm sorry to interrupt you, but the coming witness does not enjoy any protective measures, does he?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So far not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because you mentioned the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, very thoughtful of you, but I checked before I mentioned the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But don't blame me for checking because it is my responsibility to make sure that all protective measures are observed and respected at all times. Yes, sorry about the interruption, Mr. Wubben. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This means for the coming days we can fill it up with the time needed for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Any preliminary issues?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one. A small matter. We have a request to make. You know that I had some health problems and I still --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, it's not necessary. I still feel pain which is becoming more intensive when I have to stand for long periods of time. So I would like to ask the Trial Chamber if I might be allowed to examine the witness in a sitting position and as soon as I am able to examine the witnesses standing up, I shall tell you and do so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you call that a problem, Madam Vidovic, I hope that all problems will be that easy to solve. What I suggest to you, I -- of course, it's up to you whether you prefer to stay sitting where you are, or whether you would like to exchange places with Mr. Jones. It's up to you. Whichever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Anything else? Usher, please do escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Two things. First, I want to make sure that throughout the testimony, throughout the sitting, you are receiving interpretation in your language at all times. If at any moment there are problems, please draw our attention immediately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And secondly, you will notice that I am not asking you to stand up and repeat the solemn declaration, which you made last Friday. That solemn declaration still holds and of course still holds for today, for tomorrow or until you are here giving testimony. But you don't need to repeat it, because making it once is enough. Ms. Sellers will now proceed with her examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning Your Honours, learned counsel. Examined by Ms. Sellers: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask if Mr. Bogilovic might be given Prosecution Exhibit 254. I believe that is how we concluded our session on Friday. Mr. Bogilovic will be given the original and I believe the rest of us already have copies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic -- thank you. Would you please look at the document. I believe you testified last week that this order was on order that you issued together with the president of the War Presidency, Mr. Avdic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you the following question about the document. Who was the order directed to?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order came from us, and it says "We order --" We hereby order. The president of the War Presidency and myself as head of the public security service order the police to take in all illegal weapons and anything else, to confiscate them, if -- unless citizens do so themselves, and if they turn them in themselves at the nearest police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So -- [Microphone not activated]?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So he hasn't answered your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it a correct statement that this order was directed both to the ordinary citizen and as well as to the police, military or civilian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour I did want to ask that it was directed to the ordinary citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this a direct order -- looking at the body of this document, was this a direct order to the civilian and military police or a direct order to the civilians? Or anyone in possession of a firearm?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We issued the order. It was a direct order that was sent directly to anybody in possession of firearms illegally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The document may be removed right now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, just a very short question. The order only speaks of anyone in possession of a firearm, ammunition, explosive and so on, whereas in your oral statement now, you would speak of illegal weapons. That's line five, two, "illegal weapons." Again, you repeated "illegal." Now, the order, the written order seems to be broader, asking for delivering any firearm, whereas in your oral statement you speak of "illegal weapons." And if only illegal weapons, what type of weapons did you in your order think of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It means unlawfully. Anybody who did not have a permit to possess or carry a firearm, then they would have to give up those weapons, anybody unlawfully in possession of. Without permits.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic. Yes. Might I ask now -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I just -- I said thank you, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Might I ask now that the document be withdrawn from the witness and that the witness be given P5, please. And that, I'm sorry, we don't have the original. Could we please have that from the registrar. Your Honour, I would also like to thank the Defence. We informed them earlier today there were three documents that we were going to be using that weren't originally on the list and they, very graciously, are not raising an objection to that. I would like the Court to be informed of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Sellers, and I thank you, Madam Vidovic as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, please read this document in front of you now. Would you confirm to the Trial Chamber that this document was issued on the 29th of October, 1992 and, therefore, after the order that you signed that we have just discussed.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order, and the number is 9 -- I've seen this for the first time, 01239512, this place is 50 kilometers from Srebrenica. This is more a military document rather than coming under my competence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bogilovic, would you also agree that this document - in particular I want to draw your attention to the first paragraph - that the first paragraph of this document makes reference to the order that you signed and issued on the 14th of October, in that it is pursuant to order 91/92 of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this order refers exclusively to the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you agree that it is in this order that the military police are hereby ordered to carry out an investigation in relationship to the confiscation of weapons?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. And most probably this followed on because the military police -- this place is quite a long way away and at one of the meetings it was decided that two policemen should be assigned and attached to the units in the field, on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also agree that within this order that we are referring to the legal possession of weapons?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this order actually is the implementation of the earlier order that the War Presidency has set forth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because one couldn't control everything on the ground and individuals abused the situation and then, what they wanted to do was to cover the area on the ground, to introduce law and order there, on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would also agree that the military police were thereby ordered not only to implement the order to have an investigation, but they were ordered to carry it out in the different regions within the Srebrenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this referred to the entire region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, would you also confirm that the person whose name appears on the bottom right-hand side of that order is that of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as confirming that, it's the same as what I said earlier on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm only asking you at this point to confirm that is a name at the bottom of it. I'm not speaking at this point about the signature.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the name is written down here, and it says "Oric." It's typewritten and then there is a signature in Cyrillic. Now, who signed it, I really can't say. It wasn't signed in front of me for me to be able to know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it your understanding that the person's name, the person whoever signed that, did that in their capacity as a commander of the Srebrenica OS?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was -- or rather normally emanated from suspicions that individuals had -- were unlawfully in possession of weapons and I assume that this is why the order was given in the first place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Bogilovic, would you just confirm - yes or no - that the person whoever signed the order did so in their capacity as commander of the Srebrenica OS?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, I would object to that question. This witness has said this is the first time that he has seen this document. He hasn't seen this document before. He can only confirm, therefore, what is written, that it appears to have been issued on a certain date, et cetera, and so we can all see a name and a function there. As to whether he can say that it was signed in a particular function, that's beyond what this witness can testify to, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Agreed, Mr. Jones, and your objection is sustained. I mean, it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The document speaks for itself. So let's move to next the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly. Could we please remove the document from Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, you testified last Friday that, to your knowledge, Mr. Halilovic was appointed to be the commander of the military police. Can you please confirm that for us again.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that again. On the 1st of July, 1992, at the proposal of Zulfo Tursunovic [Realtime transcript read in error "Osman Osmanovic"] he was appointed commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in June of 1992, did you ever attend any of the Srebrenica staff meetings where military issues were discussed?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June I think there was one meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever --

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it was to link up the villages so that in case of an attack, that the nearest villages had the duty of raising a defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you present at a meeting in June of 19 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a small correction. The witness said that on the 1st of July, at the proposal of Zulfo Tursunovic was the name that the witness said when Halilovic was appointed commander of the military police, and the transcript says Osman Osmanovic. So it is a different name. It is Tursunovic. Could that be corrected, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, could you please direct your attention, again, to July 1st and you were speaking about the appointment of Mr. Halilovic as commander of the military police. Who, in your opinion, appointed him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was it Osman Osmanovic or Zulfo Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Not Osman Osmanovic. He wasn't there at all, as far as I remember. It was Zulfo Tursunovic who proposed Mirzet, or Mr. Halilovic, as commander of the military police on the 1st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic, for bringing that -- raising that matter, because it's important. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bogilovic, were you present in the month of June, 1992 at any of the meetings of the Srebrenica staff to discuss the appointment of Mirzet Halilovic as commander of military police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as June, certainly not. Never. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown document P4, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The witness will be given the original and I believe the rest of us will have the other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just a short question. First, the witness has been asked whether he was present and then who appointed Halilovic. And then you would say Zulfo Tursunovic suggested or proposed. There is a distinction between proposing and appointing. What was Zulfo Tursunovic doing; only proposing or appointing this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was proposing him, and we agreed that he should be commander of the military police. So we accepted that proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Might I ask the witness be shown document P4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, would you please look at the document before you. Mr. Bogilovic, do you agree, looking at the first sentence above where "order" is written, that at this time, on the 15th of June, 1992, that there was a commander of the Srebrenica staff, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here the commander was -- or rather this is a document of the 20th of May when it was first established, and then it was expanded, normally, to include Kragljivoda, Skenderovici, and Osmace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you agree that on the 15th of June, that there was a commander of the Srebrenica staff?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Srebrenica staff did exist, yes. He wasn't in Srebrenica because all of these were in their villages, in their own localities where they lived and worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you look at the part of the document that comes under section 1, "order" and can you just confirm that this document represents what your understanding was as of the 15th of June, that the Srebrenica staff was organised by Naser Oric, that Zulfo Tursunovic was part of it, and that also Ahmo Tihic and Mr. Tabakovic, and Akif Ustic were part of the Srebrenica staff, as well as Mr. Bektic.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first establishment of this took place on the 20th of May with the presence of Mr. Oric, Mr. Tursunovic, Mr. Fejzic, Mr. Bogilovic, and Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, you would understand that this document reflects that understanding that you had of the organisation, the staff during the month of June. Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The witness at no point confirmed that Naser Oric had organised the staff. He was talking about something else, that a group of people had set up the staff, but now the witness is -- it is being now suggested to the witness that he should accept that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I'm trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the objection is -- has to be sustained because he has never actually said that. You are proposing or making that proposition to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I just restate the question then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I asked: "Mr. Bogilovic, to your knowledge, was there a commander of the Srebrenica staff?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was the question that you asked before, which hasn't been answered as yet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander of the Srebrenica staff was appointed only on the 20th of May by the people when there was a mass -- when mass killings started and there was general fear and the result of all that was on the 20th of May, 1992, when this occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the Srebrenica staff as of the 20th of May?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the 20th of May, it was Mr. Oric and his deputy, Ustic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bogilovic, does this document reflect your understanding of the members of the Srebrenica staff in the month 1992? Please answer yes or no, Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Except me. Because this is military, you see.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. I have to object to this type of examination of the witness and leading him to a different content of the document than the document actually has. I would like to ask the witness to read the document or to have it read out to him, the contents of the document, which are being put to him, because what it says here is this: They struggled to win back occupied areas. Should undertake to organise and establish the units. And here, Ms. Sellers is constantly referring to the fact that it's a fait accompli, that it has already been carried out whereas the witness is saying something quite different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is precisely the question that is being put to the witness that hasn't been answered yet. Mr. Bogilovic, the question that you need to answer is the following: Looking at that list over there, does that reflect the situation as it obtained in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time that we have all these people elected by the people and that they should act and undertake the establishment of the organisation of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But does that show the position as it was in May, or as it was in June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first meeting took place on the 20th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, you have already explained to us what the outcome of that meeting was. Does this reflect the outcome of that meeting, or does it reflect the outcome of further developments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This reflects the situation which was more complex. And as it became more complex, this was expanded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So this expansion that you are referring to, is it an expansion that took place in June, 1992? Would you say that in June 1992 the expansion that you are mentioning brings us to the list that we see on this document, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Madam Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, does that expansion include -- and I would like to direct your attention to part C of this document, where, in the English version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which part C? I have part 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If one goes down to number 10, then part (c). There is (a), (b), (c).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, does this expansion also include -- in English it is: "At the VP ... the organisation to be carried out by Mirzet Halilovic."

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not quite clear on this, because Mirzet Halilovic was appointed on the 1st of July whereas this was on the 15th of June. So I'm not quite clear about this. So how could this organisation be commenced -- carried out by Mirzet Halilovic when he was appointed only as of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 1st of July?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, first I want to clarify, does "VP" mean "military police," under section (c)? Would that be your understanding?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably. It is an abbreviation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Bogilovic, is it possible that among the military meetings that occurred, that the discussion and the appointment of Mirzet Halilovic happened even though you were not present?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's supposition. He has already told us that -- stated that to his knowledge Mirzet Halilovic was appointed on the -- in July, on the 1st. So at this point in time, if there were other possibilities, he would have mentioned them already. So I would not --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I will withdraw the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, then would it be your testimony that you were unaware of any appointment of Mirzet Halilovic prior to July 1st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Again, Mr. Bogilovic, I would like to ask you to look at the bottom right-hand side of this document. Would you note that this document bears the name of Naser Oric at the bottom. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Can I see on the computer monitor, can I see what the witness is looking at?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be on the ELMO, yes. We can put that on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Okay. I am asking this -- I asked for this because the photocopy that we have would absolutely be inadequate to show to the witness, particularly if he is being asked to identify signatures, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. This, I would like to emphasise, for those reasons we have provided the originals and my question goes toward the name and not the signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, could you confirm that the name -- I'm referring to the name that is there -- is that of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this document before. Nothing was actually written up at the time. All I can do is read what it says. Same as you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Can we take the document from him. Now Your Honours, I would like to, at this point, go to Exhibit P84. I would like to inform the Trial Chamber that we have given copies of P84 in B/C/S to the interpreters so that they might have it in their hands and possibly they will be able to read directly from it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just so that you would know how to proceed, Ms. Sellers, since we started late, the break will not be at 10.30, but it will be an hour and a half after we started. So more or less we started at quarter to ten, and it will be an hour an a half from then. Unless I see objections from either the interpreters or technicians. If there are problems, please do let me know. But I don't see any.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No objection, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will be looking at pages 12 through 13 in the English version of P84, and the ERN number terminates in 5057.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: We don't have them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 5057 is on the previous page. It starts on the previous page, on page 12. So I take it you are referring to the first -- the top part, the first third of the contents of page 13, Ms. Sellers, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. As a matter of fact, I'm referring -- on the English version I have it is a meeting of October 23rd, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It starts right under ERN 5057.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's Page 12 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: We don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can put it on the ELMO. I do have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It is on Sanctions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And even though it starts on -- at that page, I want to point out the attention to Mr. Bogilovic of, in that text where it begins with "Item 1."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, are you able to read the paragraph that starts with "Item 1"?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies. Can I have some assistance from someone who is really good at reading this to read it out to me and I would be very grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Might I ask if one of the interpreters have been able to follow where we've put asterisks marked near Item 1.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that it has to be read out in the courtroom by someone first. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I might read out in English but I don't know whether that will raise the same objections that we had last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I read out Item 1A? Which portion do you want to show the witness exactly?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to show him, as a matter of fact, the second sentence in Item 1A, continuing until the end of that paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you once more, Madam Vidovic, and I wish to make it known that these gestures and -- of cooperation on the part of the Defence will not go unnoticed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Prosecution is also quite grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm only too glad to help. This sentence that the Prosecutor wants to show you is: "It was decided to order the military police to bring soldiers ... into custody and the civilian police will do the same with civilian ... First, Ahmo Tihic has to define the terms 'civilians' and 'soldiers' respectively." Is that sufficient, or should I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I want to go down to the next -- not the next paragraph, the one after that, where it says, "The security chief said ..." and then conclude with the sentence right after the next ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The security chief said that he accepted any talks or tasks put down in writing. The conclusion was adopted that an interview would be held with the military police commander at the staff headquarters regarding the functioning of the military police. "It was decided that the military police would go to Poloznik, bring into custody the guards who had refused to perform their duties, and return the requested automatic rifle."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, my question is: Were you present when these decisions were taken about the functioning of the military police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry, Ms. Sellers, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, could you answer my question, and it was: Were you present when these discussions and decisions regarding the military police were taken?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can assist the witness more by repeating to him that this meeting allegedly took place on the 23rd of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, were you present at a meeting on the 23rd of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall specifically whether I attended this meeting. This meeting was of a more military nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Bogilovic, isn't it, from your testimony, it seems that you did not attend the meetings of the military staff or military organisations.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a civilian at this time period or were you a member of the army, armed forces?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, I remained a civilian throughout. Only on the 20th of May when it was set up, since this was the first organisation that I was involved in, but after the War Presidency was set up on the 1st of July, I went back to being a civilian because the staff too was separated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, when -- at this meeting when they are discussing a conversation being held with the military police commander, they are not referring to you, are they?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they had in mind. These are military matters being discussed here, because there is reference to the military. So those implementing these conclusions, I suppose, should have been the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to have the document removed from the witness. We will be going back to that document on a couple of other occasions, but right now I would like to have document P7 shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, would you please take the time to look at this document.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this document before. I believe this is a military document. Naturally, the substance of this document is probably a military secret, though there is reference here to codes which I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Bogilovic as the chief of the republic security sector, you did not receive this document on October -- in or about October 31st, 1992. Would that be your testimony?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I wish to say. It's true that I did not receive this document, but I am really not familiar with these codes and names. The armed forces staff and then the name 1357, I have no idea what that refers to. This is all completely new to me. I don't know why these numbers are here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, I would ask you to look at the numbers 1 through 16 -- not the codes -- are you familiar that some of those names were components within the armed forces of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is not a single name here referring to a specific individual. These are code names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, I'm referring to names of brigades or battalions or places, I'm not referring to names of persons. Are you familiar with these names of brigades or battalions or units?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These references here, you mean? What things are called in the army? I know these are military matters. In Suceska and Potocari there was a military presence there, but there were no conditions there, no security provided for the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Might I draw your attention to number 16 on the list and would you agree that the military police were parts of the unit that came under the armed forces of Srebrenica as of October 31st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the document says. The line 16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Might I briefly just draw your attention to the name at the bottom of the document. Would you agree that that name is Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When we had this question, especially when we have such a poor quality, can the witness be asked: Are you able to see what name is at the bottom; and then, if so, what is it? Rather than it being suggested each time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, certainly. I understand that this part of the testimony, that I am basically making for the record. I do not want to belabour the point to be brought up around names or signatures. Now, if we do want to take it a bit slower, can you see this, or do you recognise the name? What does the name look like? Can you see the signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't think this is any way to get this witness's evidence. And the other way it's been suggested won't take that much longer to simply say: Can you identify it and what does it say? That's the correct way to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones. You are mostly correct, but not entirely. I mean, let's take it from here, Ms. Sellers. Basically, what appears on the face of the document is there for all of us -- for all of us to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I don't really see how a confirmation by the witness that at the bottom of that page it has "Commandant, Stara OS Srebrenica" and "Naser Oric," is going to improve the situation. But of course you have -- you are free to address any other question that you would like on what appears at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not for him to confirm to us what we can see for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It is particularly this one, it may be academic, but for all we know it says Oricivic [phoen] or something. We can't see the end of it, so it's artificial in the extreme to say, Do you confirm that it says Naser Oric, when in fact we can't see anything after the "I," in my submission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is the case of moving on. I can see a little bit better than you, Mr. Jones, although I do not claim to have better eyesight.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You may well have better eyesight, but that is what I can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The document may be taken away from the witness. Thank you. Your Honour. I would now ask that the witness be given document P79. I'm sorry, prior to giving the witness P79, I would just like to ask one question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, do you know someone called Osman Osmanovic, or did you know someone called Osman Osmanovic in 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally knew Mr. Osman Osmanovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me who Osman Osmanovic was and what function, if any, did he have in 1992, more precisely in the fall of 1992.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Osman Osmanovic was a teacher. He was a military person too. How he came to the staff, because that's where he worked, probably through the army, but I really can't say. He worked with the staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present, to your knowledge, at meetings of the staff in September of 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember September specifically. I was on sick leave in those days. I wasn't able to move about, so I can't be certain whether I was present or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, just for the sake of clarity, when you're referring to the "staff," are you referring to the War Presidency staff or are you referring to the military staff?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The War Presidency staff was civilian. Whenever a meeting was called, I was invited. As I was not able to come, to attend at the moment, some of the meetings were held in my absence. On the 14th of October, 1992 I was called to attend a meeting of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to September of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And could the witness please be shown document P79.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, would you please look over the document. Mr. Bogilovic, as a member of the War Presidency in September of 1992, did you ever see or receive this document?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Never. I've never seen it and I've never received it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So even though you were on the War Presidency, there were documents that were -- even though you were on the War Presidency, a document such as this might not have been given to members of the War Presidency. Would that be true?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be true. I never received it. Whether anyone else was given it, I really can't say. I hadn't ever seen this until you interviewed me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the list of names and functions between 1 and 11. Would you please look at that and see if that is familiar with your knowledge of persons and positions in September and October 1992.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with some of these names and not with others. I know Osman Osmanovic. I know Nijaz Masic, I know Adil Muhic, I know Hamed Salihovic. I'm not sure about Ibrahim Smajic, I know Ramiz Becirovic, and I know Hamed Alic. I also know Nedzib Habibovic from Krusevo [phoen]. I know Nedret Mujkanovic too. He had come from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I'm sorry, I have to intervene, because we can't go on like this. It is more confusing, the confusionary as it is. Look at the first one. Osman Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to take him through just a couple of those. I understand that he took no more than three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, because -- The other thing is that, I see here Nedzib Halilovic, but the transcript, or in the interpretation, I heard Habibovic. Did you say Nedzib Habibovic or Nedzib Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Habibovic, Nedzib.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So yes, exactly, I'm pointing this out: In the English translation of the document, there is a mistake. Because number 10 is shown as Nedzib Halilovic, while it is obvious from the original, from the -- it is Habibovic and not Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bogilovic, can we quickly confirm, if it is true, that Osman Osmanovic was the chief of operations staff, to your knowledge. Does this document reflect that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document says, Osman Osmanovic, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you also confirm that Hamed Salihovic was in the department for security and intelligence.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hamed Salihovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Because arising from the previous answer that he gave, I want to make sure whether his answer is in the sense that that's what the document states, or whether yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: To his knowledge, whether the document reflects his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that is not what he answered before. He answered that's what the document says, which is different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, to your knowledge, does this document reflect your knowledge that Hamed Salihovic was in the department of security and intelligence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honours. The witness should be asked when. Secondly, he never said he was actually aware of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But he will soon tell us whether he was aware of it, or not. And I think the first objection is relevant. I think you need to explain to the witness that this document refers to the 19th of September of 1992 and his answers ought to be restricted to that particular period.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, you do note that the date is the 19th of September. I believe my earlier question asked you, in terms of September, as a member of the War Presidency, did you have knowledge of these persons and their functions? If you didn't, you can say you didn't. If you did, certainly I would just like you to acknowledge it one way or the other, according to your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially, no. This was produced by the staff and we were not aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic. Would you please look at the last paragraph, where it says "Statement of Reason" in English, and I would like to read one line out that says: "I hereby submit it to the Presidency for verification by its decision so that it may then request approval from Republican authorities to issue decisions." Do you see that part of the document, Mr. Bogilovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says here is that they hereby submit it to the Presidency to inform the competent bodies at the republican level, most likely in order for this to be recorded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We can remove the document from the witness at this point, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, you've testified that you were at the meeting on October 14th, 1992 of the War Presidency. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it at that meeting that you became aware of certain appointments that were being made?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that when you became aware of the appointment of Osman Osmanovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then, yes, because Osman Osmanovic was occupying this position then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to have the witness shown P8, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, would you please look at this document carefully. Yes. Is this where you became aware -- does this document reflect when you became aware of the appointment of Osman Osmanovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision shows that he is being appointed, but I find it strange that it is signed by the president of the Presidency. But this same kind of document was one I received, dated the 14th of October, which was signed by the president of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you look at the document, and in particular, would you look at section 5. According to your knowledge, who did Osman Osmanovic report to as a superior?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to this decision, Osman Osmanovic should have reported to the commander of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your appointment as chief of public security, who did you report to?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was subordinated to the president of the War Presidency, Hajrudin Avdic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to your knowledge, during that time period Osman Osmanovic reported to a military line of command and you reported to a civilian line of command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The same thing was repeated that we had on Friday. The witness at no point said that a chain of command existed. That is something that was suggested and is being constantly suggested to him by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I could rephrase that as a superior. I'm not trying to imply in any way in establishing a command. I'm just trying to say who one would report to, in that sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that was made clear last time and that is how it is being taken today. The witness's answer does not really indicate or is being taken as meaning that there was -- there was a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. confirmation that there was a proper chain of command. It's a question of who he was answerable to. All right. I mean, I'm pretty sure that he knows who he was answerable to in any case. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to have the document to be taken, I would like to direct the attention of Mr. Bogilovic to the screen and our attention also. There is a photo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, do you recognise any of the persons in this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The microphone, witness microphone. One is switched on, the other one isn't, but he is speaking over the one which is not switched on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do recognise Osman Osmanovic and Mr. Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to explain this. First of all, one moment, Mr. Bogilovic. Which exhibit is this clip taken from, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is also 517. This is the same video that we used on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness is being shown a clip from or a still from exhibit -- Prosecution Exhibit P517. The still occurring at, clocked at 2 minutes 56 seconds point 7. And the clip also shows a date of 19th of August, 1992, with the time shown at 8.30. 8.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that is 2.55.7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What did I say? 2.56? Yes, it is 2.55. Two minutes 55 seconds, point 7. Now, Witness, you said you recognised two persons. But I see three. Could you identify the two persons one by one, please. Do you identify the person that you see on the extreme left of the document? You see an arrow pointing at that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where the arrow is, that's Mr. Osman Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the record, the witness has indicated the person to be Osman Osmanovic as the person which is -- who is at the extreme left of the screen. Let's move to the one in the middle. Do you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where the arrow is now is Mr. Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And for the record, the witness has identified the person who stands in the middle, in the centre of this still, as being Naser Oric. And let's put the arrow on the third person. Look at that person. Do you identify that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The arrow on the person is a person I don't know. I cannot recognise that individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And for the record, the person that the witness is unable to identify is the person at the extreme right of the photo. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours. We may dispense now with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, at the meeting on the 14th of October, 1992, to your memory were there any announcements in regard to Mr. Hamed Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was officially appointed to a position, or not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day there were a number of decisions that were made, so I really can't say for each individual. I can't confirm. I'm not sure. Probably there are the minutes that were kept in the notebook, and you could find it there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would there also possibly be other types of documents similar to the one that you received in regard to your appointment?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can guarantee from my document, the one I received. As for others, what the procedure was there, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have the witness see document 221. Prosecution Exhibit 221. We have the translation. I don't know whether the others have it. We would be willing to hand it up. If the usher could please assist us also with the translations that we would like to have handed to the Trial Chamber and the parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, looking at this document, does that refresh your memory in regard to Mr. Salihovic on the 14th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as this format is concerned and this decision, I received the same thing. It looked like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was Mr. Salihovic appointed as chief of intelligence and security affairs during that time period?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I don't know military terms well enough, I can't say who did what function. But all I can say is that he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, from your knowledge, who Mr. Salihovic would have reported to as a superior?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he was with the army, then that should have been to the military command. He should have been subordinated to the military command. But I'm not sure because everything is being mixed up here. Once again, I see Hajrudin Avdic's signature here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that signature, Mr. Bogilovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Signatures like this, what can I say?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You can remove the document from the witness. Your Honours, I now go to P84 again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to pages 16, in the English version, through 17, and the ERN number would be 02115063. If one would go to page 17 now in the English version, where it says: "A meeting of the 3rd of November 1992." Mr. Bogilovic, you've consistently testified that you were not present during military meetings or when military matters were discussed. I would like to have a section read out to you again, to ask you, are you aware of the contents of this discussion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, might I ask you -- is it possible you can remain seated while reading?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm concerned with the paragraph that begins with the English version, "The Chief and Ramiz B." then it concludes in the next paragraph down with the very -- what appears to be a short paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "In addition to the chief of staff, in addition to the chief of staff, the meeting of the War Presidency will be attended by Becir [as interpreted] B. Ramiz. The meeting doesn't have an agenda, but from the announcement we can conclude that two police forces will function, the present communications and information service and current issues will be discussed. When it comes to the civilian and military police, the staff maintains it is necessary to carry out personnel changes. All former policemen, both active duty and reserve, must be included in both forces. Insists that record be made of all confiscated items and one copy be given to the owner of the confiscated item. Both police forces must inform the order issuing authority that the order has been carried out."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. I saw in the transcript that it says "Becir." It is "B. Ramiz."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bogilovic, you have just listened to that part of this document being read out. Now, were you aware of these discussions taking place at the meetings, the military meetings concerning the police organisations?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something that is linked to military meetings? Well, if I wasn't there, I became aware of it only if Avdic told me about it. Ramiz is mentioned here and it is Becirovic Ramiz that is referred to and the B. is the abbreviation. But it is Becirovic. B. is short for Becirovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic. Can we clarify something: Was the entire organisation of the military police put under your authority or was it Mirzet Halilovic who was placed under you after October 14th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 14th of October, 1992, under my competence and authority, Mirzet was placed -- it said Mirzet. That is what was written, Mirzet. Now it didn't say for the others. All it said was Mirzet, and he was the commander of the military police at the time, komandir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to draw your attention to, I believe we remain with P84 and we'll look at pages in the English version, 19 through 20. The ERN number concludes in 5068. I draw your attention next to the minutes of the 9th of November, 1992 meeting. Mr. Bogilovic, did you attend a joint meeting of the War Presidency and the armed forces staff on the 9th of November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that at that meeting on the agenda was to be a discussion about the police force?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a rather broad meeting and everything was discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that meeting, do you remember whether you participated in discussions concerning the safety and security concerns in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as Zepa is concerned, that was a problem that they had made because they issued an order to Zepa that all the people there, for their own safety and security, should move into the Srebrenica area. So that created a great influx of citizens coming in, which disrupted law and order where we were and created problems for us. So of course we discussed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discuss also the safety concerns of the forces, the armed forces that would go to Zepa? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember. Now, whether it was my job -- well, the safety and security of citizens was -- I think I proposed that at distant points, especially Zepa where it was unsafe, you had to go on foot for 12 hours and the Serb forces would cut across the terrain. So for that reason, I proposed, as -- that as commander, Mr. Oric should not go because he was needed here, because most of the people was there -- were there, in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I draw your attention to page 20 in the English version. And I just would like to confirm. It is one sentence, if I could be allowed just to read that sentence and have it translated. Mr. Bogilovic, did you say something of the nature that: "It was agreed that our commander would not go there. He can only go when the security conditions are better." Do you agree that you said something of that nature at the meeting concerning security concerns in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably I did say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to draw your attention to page 21 in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Here I would have to ask for some assistance. Again, there is a rather longer passage. It is found under ERN number 5070. If I could ask for some assistance from Madam Vidovic again. I would like to have the witness read where about one-half way down the page, it says "Sahid," and then on the second line it says "Osman." If we could read from there and then conclude.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Sahid: I'm not trying to defend myself. I'm going to say exactly what is not good. "Osman: At first, everything was okay with the police. When we 'illegally' changed the composition of the police force, problems arise. The military police do not have any support. "Hamdija: There is still some shooting. When this is not done properly, everything goes downhill. In these matters we should start from the commander. "Becir: We are all being dishonest. We are also to blame. Units are stealing from other units. If a vehicle belongs to the Armed Forces and if somebody is a member... the civilian police do not have the right to intervene. "Conclusion: File a report against the unit commander and pass it to the Staff. "The court is not functioning. We do not have a state or authorities so we have to do best we can. Troublemakers should be detained for three days and then put on trial! "The military police and civilian police --" and here it is not quite clear -- "include --" and then the part that isn't clear. "Hamed: We have the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It's better to have some kind of government than none at all. I propose: - That the Secretariat designate the military posts. - That the Secretariat work out wartime assignments for everyone. - The Police should be assigned tasks according to a staff specification. "Osman: We need an internal act for the military police. There are enough men for the reserve police force as well. Take the VES -- VES/VP -- military police from the files. "Zulfo: We have to pass regulations until freedom. Let's punish the offenders: The court cannot pass final judgments. It has not been formed properly. It has a preventative task. "- The military police belongs to the OSA not VP. - Work out the VES. - 90% of the policemen to be from the Srebrenica area. - Work out a job classification description of other duties for the police. "Mirza: You gave me a free hand. ... two months. Is that all right? But somebody didn't like the town having been put in order -- people from Potocari. The new people that I got were worse. - People must be appointed at the next meeting and this should be set up, set up checkpoints. They should be manned by members of both police forces. - Three vehicles must be requisitioned - everything socially-owned - from private entrepreneurs." And then we have a paragraph entitled "Information."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I am very grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, was it clear that problems arising both in the civilian and in the military police were discussed by both the military staff and War Presidency staff at this joint meeting?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, yes. Because there were many problems that had amassed. Lots of things hadn't been solved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these problems were well known at this time, weren't they, Mr. Bogilovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they did crop up, yes, because people from other areas were coming in, inhabitants from other areas were coming in. And the more people who were coming in, the larger the problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in what has just been read to you, there was a name that was Mirza. What is the full name of that person, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was Halilovic, Mirza, I think his real name was Mirzet and he was called Mirza for short, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mirzet or Mirza Halilovic disagreed with the fact that you would have any authority over him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he answered that question last Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He explained, from what I recall, that this Halilovic ignored him, he wanted to go his own way, and that he had to write a long letter to Avdic as a result of which then Halilovic was removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then can I just go directly to the quote that is attributed to Mirzet here. Does that also reflect some of the antagonism that he felt, particularly toward you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you need to repeat the question, because I noticed that the witness dropped his earphones while you were --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Mr. Mirzet's quote read that, "You gave me a free hand. Everything was good for two months. But somebody didn't like it, that the town has been put in order -- people from Potocari. The new people that I got were worse." Would you agree that some of the antagonism that Mr. Halilovic might have felt towards you was contained in that statement?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably that was his defence. It all depended on how he dealt with the situation in town, whether he did this -- did his duty in the prescribed manner, or not. So quite normally individuals didn't like it, whereas his people, his men probably liked it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to move to page 23 of P84.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I understand we're coming up to a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You've got roughly two minutes. If you can finish the next question in two minutes, go ahead. If not, we'll have a break now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, let's go to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 25-minute break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 11:55 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please be seated. Sorry for the delay. We had a technical problem. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, in October and November 1992, was the civilian police charged with setting up any checkpoints or barriers within the town in the municipality of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please speak a little closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe so. That was the reason someone had to bring order, to create an entrance to the street, and all those coming in had to be registered. There were difficulties with motor vehicles, motor vehicles coming in and the people driving them were not the actual owners. And sometimes owners would turn up with valid permits and papers showing that those were their vehicles. So in order to be able to return these vehicles to their rightful owners, we set up a swing gate so that people on the way in could be registered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that manned by the civilian police or the military police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think all of us were civilians because we dealt with civilians and the military dealt with their own.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to go back to P84 now. And in the English version, it is page 23, ERN number ends in 5073.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you nearly finished your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would truly like to finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please try because we want to make sure that this witness goes home on Wednesday. Finishes on Wednesday, anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, if I just may ask you, were you present at the meeting on the 10th of November, 1992 of the OS staff?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the date. But if indeed I was present, most probably I would have contributed. I did every time I was there, so if this is actually recorded in the minutes, then I must have been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you normally attend the meetings of the OS, the military staff, Mr. Bogilovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention now to page 24 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And if I might ask the indulgence of defence counsel again, on page 24, where we have more than halfway down Zulfo starts to speak, until the end of where Mirza speaks, if that could be read out to Mr. Bogilovic. The ERN number on that page would be -- would end in 5074.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Zulfo: Top priority is to put the police on a sound footing. "Ramiz: An order will be issued prohibiting soldiers from moving around without their cards or leave permits. The police must have the right to carry out checks both in town and at the checkpoint. All reports shall be submitted to the Staff. The police must register all the vehicles and some of these are to be given to units for use. "Avdic: Vehicles must be requisitioned and given to units. Three to five vehicles have to be parked outside the Staff. "Osman: All vehicles must be requisitioned. "Mirza: After the meeting at the Cultural Centre, I waited for an order to set up checkpoints and carry out checks. The checkpoints have still not been set up."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would then now like to go to page 25 where it says section II, and if we could just have the first paragraph after section II read out to Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Cooperation with the military police is good. The composition and numbers of personnel in the military police should be permanent. The idea about deployment along the front line and stepping in are Mirza's. The chief of the public security station has not passed on the order to set up barricades to the police. As for requisitioning material and technical equipment from the population, everything went well in the beginning. There are surely people in the police for whom bringing order would not be convenient. It is important for us to have a strong police force. Whichever policemen cooperated with commanders were good policemen -- to find the perpetrators of the latest incidents. "Zulfo: There are some individuals who do not find it convenient to have good police officers around."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, my question is: Did you issue orders to Mirza Halilovic to set up the checkpoints during this time period? This is November 1992.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I issued any orders for checkpoints to be set up. This would need to be set up by one of the civilian authorities in order to check citizens on their way in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would now just like to have part of that same page - and I would like to remind us we're on ERN 0211075, where it starts with "carry out an investigation," on that second line is the word "Mirza." Madam Vidovic, if you are able to?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please -- can you please repeat the reference number, the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The ERN number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, it's two lines from where you left before. Two lines from where you stopped reading before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "He did not let Ahmo's men go to the prison for 48 hours and is no longer with the police. - Conduct an investigation into that fellow from Bajramovici's... Mirza says that he has carried out the preliminary procedure, and the record was delivered to Becir. Mirza was not supposed to put him in gaol. Resid or Hamed and the court to conduct further proceedings. Suspects to be detained. The police are ... opening up checkpoints. The police to be revitalised by Suljo."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, my question is were you working with Mirza then in detaining or arresting persons who committed crimes in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that Ahmo Tihic brought some persons in.
